correctness.rationale: The complete square is the exact family of four-side tangent ellipses. For a fixed point the admissible k interval has length twice sqrt((1-x^2)(1-y^2)) and lies in [-1,1] by Cauchy–Schwarz. Independent m-fold coverage and Tonelli give the beta-square mean-area formula, with gamma-quotient asymptotic. The pairwise formula follows by exact radial integration across a single angle cut; subtraction of equations gives exactly four transverse real intersections. 205 numerical quadrature checks corroborate the area formula and incidence; finite computation is not the proof.

value.rationale: The side-contact-uniform measure is geometrically canonical and affine-invariant across every parallelogram. The result solves the complete integer-m expected-overlap hierarchy, including a surprising shape-independent 4/9 fraction and sharp 1/m decay, and provides a usable complete closed two-parameter deterministic intersection kernel and crossing rigidity. These are motivated quantitative intersection invariants, not arbitrary special-case constants or known-table recomputations.
